problem: sort() now returns list(ivs) without sorting, but merge() assumes input sorted by lower bound (closed first at ties), so normalize/union/intersection/difference silently lose or corrupt intervals on unsorted input.
No tests exist for unsorted input or mixed open/closed lower-bound ordering, so the ordering regression is undetected.
complement() requires a merged, sorted list but does not check it, so it now yields wrong gaps when the removed sort leaves merge() input unsorted.
